name: Main tower groups
kicker: Cham brick towers in a forested valley
summary: Cham brick towers in a closed valley: walk groups B, C, and D on a morning from Hoi An. A non-resident adult ticket is 150,000 VND. Visiting runs to 18:00, and an older close of 17:00 is also published, so come early. Skip the morning if brick ruins are the wrong day.
getThere: 45 km by road from Hoi An
heroCaption: Brick towers in the valley, with the mountain behind

notice.title: Come in the morning
notice.body: Ticket sales run until 17:30 and visiting ends at 18:00. An older notice closes the site at 17:00. Use the morning.

body: Stop at the museum by the Khe Thẻ stream, then take the electric cart. The ride is about 2 km, and it is included in the entrance ticket. French surveys recorded 72 structures in 13 lettered groups. About 20 towers still stand, mostly in B, C, and D. Tower A1, once 24 meters, came down in the 1969 bombing. More than 40 temple structures remain relatively intact, along with the enclosure walls. UNESCO counts eight groups and 71 monuments at inscription. Walk the groups that are open.

Each group sits inside a thick brick wall. The main tower usually opens to the east. A few large towers also have a west door. A gate tower stands in front, then a long hall with a tile roof, where pilgrims left offerings and the dances were held. The styles in the valley are Mỹ Sơn E1, Hòa Lai, Đồng Dương, Mỹ Sơn A1, Ponaga, and Bình Định, in fired brick and sandstone. The walls are the brick. Door frames, lintels, and the altar stones are the sandstone. Tower B1 is the one with a stone base. The linga from B1 is in the museum. The linga and yoni that still stand in the open are a different stone. In group B, an original wall of tower B4 dates to the 9th century, in the Đồng Dương style.

Group G is the Italian restoration. Experts surveyed the valley from 1997 to 2000, and Italy funded the work with UNESCO’s backing. The daytime show is at the foot of that group, and the brick there also uses laterite. Tower E7 is a boat-roofed kosagrha, restored from 2011 to 2015, with one of the most intact roofs of that type. Bomb fragments found when A1 was cleared are displayed in tower D2, and reliefs are kept inside D1 and D2. Stay on the paths. Leave the brick unclimbed, leave food outside the monument area, and leave the flash off the stone. Unidentified unexploded ordnance is still recorded in the buffer zone.

gettingThere: Cars stop at the museum. An electric cart covers about 2 km along the Khe Thẻ stream, and that ride is inside the entrance ticket. There is no train into the valley. Tourism bus 01DL, from Hoi An, is paused for six months from 15 Sep 2026.

legs.heading: From Hoi An
legs.body: By road, 45 km. Hire a car. Bus 01DL is paused from 15 Sep 2026 for six months.

legs.heading: From Da Nang
legs.body: By road, 68 km from the city. The airport is a further ride on top of that distance.

hours: Opens at 06:00. Ticket sales run until 17:30. Visiting ends at 18:00. An older notice closes the site at 17:00.
closed: Open every day, including holidays. Bad weather can stop the show at group G.
admissionNote: A non-resident adult is listed at 150,000 VND and a Vietnamese adult at 100,000 VND, including VAT. The purchase page showed 148,000 VND and 99,000 VND on 21 Oct 2026. Read the amount before you pay. The ticket covers the museum, the electric cart, a Cham folk performance, and the monuments. Children from 5 to 15 buy the 30,000 VND shuttle ticket. Children under 5 are free. An on-site explanation is 100,000 VND for one to five guests. The green bicycle, the audio guide, pottery, and hat-weaving have no published price.
